title: More 1936-38 personnel: Gus Wilson, Ike Covington, Bill Hahnot, Eugene Porter
summary: The brothers recall Gus Wilson's inability to settle down, Ike Covington, Bill Hahnot after Blanton, and Eugene Porter joining.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: We had -- we forgot to mention Gus
Wilson. We had in the band.
We had Gus Wilson in the band and we had Ike Covington.
Yeah, Ike Covington, yeah. Out of --
He was out of Philadelphia.
Out of Philadelphia, yeah. Used to write for some of the acts, huh?
Uh-huh, they're good -- Wilson was in that '36 deal, but he and Chester Lane -- when Booker came in, you know, we all live on --
That's right, that's right. In 1936, Gus Wilson the brother of Teddy Wilson was with our band, and with Gus we never could get him to really settle down and, in a business like way --
He could never relax --

Right, he could never relax. He just -- he was too far gone. He was just -- nice guy -- one of the nicest persons you'd ever know, but just -- he just couldn't shake what was wrong with him, he just couldn't shake it.
Hayes, when was Bill Hatnot in there?
Bill Hatnot -- Bill Hatnot, came in after Blanton had gone.
After -- after Blanton?
After Blanton, yes.
Yeah, that's right. Uh-huh.
Yes.
I was living down on West (unintelligible).
Bill Hahot came with the band after Blanton, now that must've -- Bill Hahot, see in '38, was when -- did Bill Hahot go to Cincinnati with us?
That's what I'm trying -- that's what I'm trying to think, Yeah, I think he did. I believe he did.
Yes he did.
There's that personnel, changes that again, too. You had Eugene Porter in the band with you in Cincinnati, you know.
That's right. We had Eugene Porter, a very fine tenor saxophonist and an excellent clarinet player.
